cases.question: Which units are vacant right now?
cases.title: Vacant Units Right Now
cases.sql:
SELECT 
    b.name AS building_name, 
    u.unit_number, 
    u.unit_type, 
    u.bedrooms, 
    u.sqft, 
    u.monthly_rent 
FROM unit u 
JOIN building b ON u.building_id = b.building_id 
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 
    FROM lease l 
    JOIN lease_status ls ON l.status_id = ls.status_id 
    WHERE l.unit_id = u.unit_id AND ls.is_current = 1
)
ORDER BY b.name, u.unit_number;
assumptions: A unit is vacant if it does not currently have an active lease (where the lease status has is_current = 1).

cases.question: List tenants who currently have a lease, with their unit and monthly rent.
cases.title: Tenants with Current Leases, Units, and Monthly Rent
cases.sql:
SELECT 
    t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS tenant_name,
    u.unit_number AS unit,
    u.monthly_rent AS monthly_rent,
    ls.label AS lease_status
FROM tenant t
JOIN lease l ON t.tenant_id = l.tenant_id
JOIN unit u ON l.unit_id = u.unit_id
JOIN lease_status ls ON l.status_id = ls.status_id
WHERE ls.is_current = 1
ORDER BY t.last_name, t.first_name
assumptions: Currently having a lease includes leases with status Active - Fixed Term, Active - Month to Month, and Notice Given (as defined by current lease statuses).

cases.question: How many maintenance requests are still open in each building?
cases.title: Open Maintenance Requests by Building
cases.sql: SELECT b.name AS building_name, COUNT(m.request_id) AS open_requests FROM building b JOIN unit u ON b.building_id = u.building_id JOIN maintenance m ON u.unit_id = m.unit_id WHERE m.state = 'open' GROUP BY b.building_id, b.name ORDER BY open_requests DESC
assumptions: Maintenance requests are considered open when their state is 'open'.
Buildings with zero open maintenance requests are not shown.

cases.question: Which tenants paid rent late at least once in 2026?
cases.title: Tenants Who Paid Rent Late at Least Once in 2026
cases.sql: SELECT DISTINCT t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS tenant_name, t.email, t.phone FROM tenant t JOIN lease l ON t.tenant_id = l.tenant_id JOIN payment p ON l.lease_id = p.lease_id WHERE strftime('%Y', p.due_on) = '2026' AND p.paid_on > p.due_on ORDER BY t.last_name, t.first_name
assumptions: Late payment is defined as a payment where paid_on is after due_on.
Payments in 2026 are determined by their due_on date falling in the year 2026.

cases.question: Total rent collected per region in 2026.

questions.question: Should the rent collected in 2026 be based on when the payment was paid or when it was due?
options: Payments actually paid in 2026 (based on payment date)
Payments due in 2026 (based on due date)

cases.question: Urgent maintenance requests that are not closed, with the technician assigned.
cases.title: Urgent Maintenance Requests Not Closed
cases.sql: SELECT m.request_id AS request_id, b.name AS building_name, u.unit_number AS unit_number, m.category AS category, m.state AS state, m.opened AS opened_date, s.first_name || ' ' || s.last_name AS technician_name FROM maintenance m JOIN unit u ON m.unit_id = u.unit_id JOIN building b ON u.building_id = b.building_id LEFT JOIN staff s ON m.assigned_to = s.staff_id WHERE m.priority = 'urgent' AND m.state != 'closed'
assumptions: Urgent maintenance requests means records where priority is 'urgent'.
Not closed means state is not equal to 'closed'.
Assigned technician is retrieved from the staff table based on assigned_to ID.

cases.question: Average number of days to close a plumbing request.
cases.title: Average Days to Close Plumbing Requests
cases.sql:
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG(julianday(closed) - julianday(opened)), 1) AS average_days_to_close,
    COUNT(*) AS closed_plumbing_requests_count
FROM maintenance 
WHERE category = 'plumbing' 
  AND state = 'closed'
assumptions: Only closed plumbing requests are included in the average calculation
Days to close is calculated as the difference between the closed date and the opened date

cases.question: Leases ending between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31.
cases.title: Leases Ending Between October and December 2026
cases.sql: SELECT l.lease_id, t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS tenant_name, u.unit_number, l.start_date AS start_date, l.end_date AS end_date FROM lease l JOIN tenant t ON l.tenant_id = t.tenant_id JOIN unit u ON l.unit_id = u.unit_id WHERE l.end_date BETWEEN '2026-10-01' AND '2026-12-31'
assumptions: Leases are considered ending between the given dates if their end date falls within the range inclusive.

cases.question: Which buildings have an elevator and more than 10 units?
cases.title: Buildings with an Elevator and More Than 10 Units
cases.sql: SELECT b.name AS building_name, b.street, b.city, COUNT(u.unit_id) AS unit_count FROM building b JOIN unit u ON b.building_id = u.building_id WHERE b.has_elevator = 1 GROUP BY b.building_id HAVING COUNT(u.unit_id) > 10
assumptions: Buildings with an elevator are represented by has_elevator = 1.
More than 10 units means unit count > 10.

cases.question: Evicted tenants and their email addresses.
cases.title: Evicted Tenants and Their Email Addresses
cases.sql:
SELECT
  tenant.first_name AS "First Name",
  tenant.last_name AS "Last Name",
  tenant.email AS Email
FROM tenant
JOIN lease ON tenant.tenant_id = lease.tenant_id
JOIN lease_status ON lease.status_id = lease_status.status_id
WHERE lease_status.label = 'Evicted'
assumptions: Evicted tenants are those whose lease status is 'Evicted'.
